verdict_reason: This is a proxy-only task with no source paper, so the reference is its own documented estimand: cosine geometry over embedding rows. Four of the five kernel families now honour that exactly. Rescaling gpt2's whole embedding table by 1e-20 -- a transformation under which every cosine is invariant by definition -- leaves ALL 14 purity values, all 14 purity_matched values, all 9 hub_skew/hub_max values, both relation consistencies and all four analogy accuracies bit-identical (e.g. seasons_purity 0.4894736842105263, punctuation_hub_skew 1.6976149564243423, present_past_analogy_acc_top5 0.54), because they route through `safe_unit_rows`. `_compute_separation` does NOT: it still calls `scipy.spatial.distance.cosine` on float32 rows (categories.py:174, 182), which squares before summing, and under the same 1e-20 rescale EVERY `<cat>_intra`, `<cat>_inter` and `<cat>_separation` value for all 14 categories collapses to exactly 0.0 -- seasons goes 0.525458 / 0.755277 / 0.229819 -> 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0. The scipy kernel returns exactly 0.0 for float32 rows at any scale <= 1e-19 where the true cosine distance is 0.9587836. This is the same defect class the round-2 corrections removed from the other five sites in this file and that `tests/test_scale_invariance.py` pins for the sibling kernels; the separation branch was missed and has no test.
comparable_reason: The task states this itself (`cross_model_comparable: False`, `comparability_note: tokenizer_dependent_category_token_mapping`) and the measurements confirm it is not a small effect. Over six models the category populations differ: `digits` maps to 20 tokens on GPT-2/Pythia/gpt2-medium but only 10 on SmolLM2, whose k_eff falls 19 -> 9 and whose digits_purity is consequently 1.0000 against 0.4395-0.5605 for every other model -- a ceiling artifact, not geometry. Across the 11 categories whose token count varies over the panel, Spearman(|rho|) between a category's token count and its purity averages 0.620. Worse, the taxonomy is not a PARTITION: 7 words and 14 gpt2 token ids belong to two categories (this/that/these/those/their/your in determiners AND pronouns; 'in' in prepositions AND units) and are assigned first-wins in `categories.json` dict order. Swapping the `pronouns` and `determiners` keys in the asset -- which changes nothing about the model -- moves pronouns_purity 0.400735 -> 0.306250 (-23.6%), determiners_purity 0.206818 -> 0.301786 (+45.9%), pronouns_purity_matched 0.055556 -> 0.122222 (+120.0%), and their token counts 68/44 -> 56/56.
normalized_variant: <category>_purity_matched (all 14; fixed m = 10 and k = 9, blake2b-seeded subsample; NORMALIZERS has 0 entries)
github_reason: No code was ever released because there is no introducing paper: task_metadata.py records `geometry_categories` as 'proxy-only', reference 'BLME category geometry', with an EMPTY repository field, and the 491-line module cites none. The nearest external references for the individual kernels (Mikolov-style analogy accuracy, k-occurrence hubness after Radovanovic et al.) are conventions rather than a released implementation of THIS composite. NONE is the accurate answer. In place of parity I used independent reimplementations: an exact-cosine reference for purity/separation, an independent k-occurrence recomputation for hubness, and scipy.stats.skew for the skew.
paper_reason: There is no source paper and therefore no published value for any of the 106 feature-eligible keys this task emits. The BLME manuscript carries it as one catalogue row with no equation. The reproducible anchors are constructed rather than published, and they pass: orthogonal clusters give separation 1.000000 and adaptive purity 1.000000; exactly parallel relation difference vectors give consistency 1.0 and analogy top-1/top-5 = 1.0/1.0; and every one of those is unchanged under an embedding rescale by 1e-20 (the separation anchor excepted -- see the verdict).
confounds_reason: The confound is the tokenizer, and it is direct rather than statistical. `n_category_tokens_mapped` is 718/718/725/725/718/665 across gpt2/distilgpt2/pythia-70m/pythia-160m/gpt2-medium/SmolLM2-135M with Spearman rho(vocab) = +1.000 exactly. Per category the effect is larger than any geometric signal: SmolLM2's `digits` maps to 10 tokens against 20 elsewhere and reads purity 1.0000 against 0.4395-0.5605; `seasons` maps to 18-22 tokens and k_eff 17-20. Mean |Spearman| between a category's token count and its purity is 0.620 over the 11 categories with varying counts. Width and depth are NOT the mechanism (the kernels are cosines over embedding rows, dimension-free), and the label-collision test above shows an equally large sensitivity to the ASSET's key order.
defects: CODE/FIDELITY, categories.py:174 and 182: `_compute_separation` uses `scipy.spatial.distance.cosine` on float32 rows, which forms `np.dot(u,u)` and `np.dot(v,v)` in float32 and underflows. It returns exactly 0.0 for two nonzero float32 vectors at any scale <= 1e-19 where the true cosine distance is 0.9587836, and end to end on gpt2 an embedding rescale by 1e-20 collapses all 42 intra/inter/separation values to 0.0 while the other 40 emitted values are bit-identical. `safe_unit_rows` is already imported in this module and used at four other sites.

CODE, categories.py:290-292: `_compute_hubness` maps a zero-variance occurrence histogram to 0.0, but `scipy.stats.skew` on a constant array returns NaN. The sibling `geometry_hubness` was changed in round 3 to propagate NaN and its parity test now pins that against scipy; `geometry_categories` still fabricates 0.0, which is a legal skew value meaning 'symmetric', for an undefined statistic.

DATA/ESTIMAND, src/blme/assets/categories.json: the taxonomy is not a partition. 7 words (this, that, these, those, their, your, in) and 14 gpt2 token ids belong to two categories, resolved first-wins in dict order. Reordering two keys moves pronouns_purity -23.6%, determiners_purity +45.9% and pronouns_purity_matched +120.0% with the model untouched. Either de-duplicate the asset or make multi-label membership explicit.

CODE/GLOBAL STATE, categories.py:153, 351, 435: three `np.random.seed(42)` calls on the GLOBAL legacy numpy RNG, one of them INSIDE the per-category loop of `_compute_relation_consistency`, so every relation category draws the same 200 analogy index pairs and any later task in the same process inherits a reset global stream. Every other seeded site in this file (the matched-purity subsample) already uses `np.random.default_rng`.

PROTOCOL, categories.py:161-184: `inter` draws 100 non-category tokens and then uses only `random_tids[:10]`. Over 30 independent 10-token draws on gpt2, seasons_inter has sd 0.008076 (range 0.733382-0.767256), i.e. 3.5% of the emitted `seasons_separation` of 0.229819 comes from the control draw alone; no uncertainty is reported. `inter` is also not a between-CATEGORY contrast -- it is category-vs-random-vocabulary -- despite the name.

PROTOCOL, categories.py:358-367: analogy pairs are enumerated exhaustively only for n < 20 and otherwise sampled 200 times WITH replacement via `np.random.choice(n, 2, replace=False)` inside a loop, so the two relation categories (gpt2: singular_plural n=21, present_past n=49) score a random subset with duplicates rather than all n(n-1) ordered pairs.
